title: FancyZones: Snap to last known zone fails with some apps
summary: FancyZones last-known-zone placement is deterministic but application-dependent: Visual Studio opens a few pixels offset, while additional Explorer and Terminal windows are not restored to the exact prior zone on a three-monitor system.

judgment.rationale: The report gives a clear feature setting, repeatable sequence, affected and unaffected applications, exact placement symptoms, and monitor topology. Maintainer-side reproduction should compare initial window rectangles and post-creation repositioning for apps that restore their own placement.
evidence: Move newly created windows to their last known zone is enabled.
Visual Studio 2022/2026 opens offset a few pixels to the right.
Explorer and Terminal only place the first window reliably; additional concurrent windows land approximately in the region.
VS Code, Excel, Rider, Settings, Edge, Outlook, Teams, and Chrome reportedly behave correctly.
The primary monitor is 3440x1440 at 100% scaling with two additional monitors at different resolutions.
judgment.recommended_action: Reproduce with Visual Studio, Explorer, and Terminal while tracing the initial and delayed window-position events against FancyZones last-known-zone placement.

fix_assessment.rationale: The application-specific pattern suggests FancyZones placement is being overwritten or rounded by later app-owned window restoration, but event tracing is needed to select the correct stabilization point.

proposed_fixes.title: Stabilize last-known-zone placement after app-owned window restoration
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Likely a race or coordinate-conversion mismatch between FancyZones initial placement and application-owned restore/reposition behavior for multi-instance or DPI-aware windows.
plan: Trace WinEvent location changes and placement calls from window creation through the first settled rectangle for the affected apps.
Compare logical/physical coordinate conversion and work-area offsets on the mixed-monitor topology.
If the app overwrites the initial placement, defer or reapply the saved zone only at the established new-window stabilization boundary without fighting normal user moves.
Add targeted coverage for multiple windows sharing the same executable and saved zone.
verification: Open sequential and concurrent Visual Studio, Explorer, and Terminal windows and confirm each settles exactly in the saved zone without pixel drift.
Verify unaffected apps and mixed-DPI monitor transitions do not regress.

confidence.rationale: The affected/unaffected app split and pixel offset point to placement timing or coordinate conversion, but runtime traces are required to distinguish them.

issue_context.summary: Last-known-zone restoration is inaccurate for several apps despite working for others on the same mixed-monitor setup.
known_information: PowerToys 0.98.1 installed with WinGet on Windows 11 Enterprise 24H2.
Visual Studio shows a small horizontal offset.
Additional Explorer and Terminal windows do not consistently occupy the exact saved zone.
inferences: Some affected applications may perform a later window-placement update after FancyZones acts.
The Visual Studio pixel drift may involve work-area or DPI coordinate conversion.
issue_context.analysis: The report is sufficiently specific for targeted maintainer reproduction. Comparing the full window-position event sequence across affected and unaffected apps will distinguish an app-owned late move from a shared coordinate calculation error.
initial_investigation: Compared affected and unaffected application groups and the supplied mixed-monitor topology.
Identified window-placement timing and coordinate conversion as the two discriminating hypotheses.

actions.label: Approve last-known-zone placement stabilization design

design.title: Approve last-known-zone placement stabilization design
design.prompt: Design a focused fix for PowerToys issue 50633. Trace FancyZones last-known-zone placement from window creation through settled app-owned repositioning for Visual Studio, Explorer, and Terminal on mixed-monitor layouts; distinguish delayed app restoration from coordinate conversion, then stabilize placement and add multi-instance coverage.

actions.note: Approval starts fork-side design work only; no upstream write occurs automatically.

reproduce.version: Current main and PowerToys 0.98.1 for comparison
prerequisites: Enable Move newly created windows to their last known zone
Use a three-monitor setup including 3440x1440 at 100% scaling
Install Visual Studio, Windows Terminal, and use File Explorer
steps: Snap one affected application window into a FancyZones zone.
Open another window while the first remains open and record its initial and settled rectangles.
Repeat after closing the first window and after restarting PowerToys.
Repeat for Visual Studio, Explorer, Terminal, and one unaffected control application.
reproduce.expected: Every newly created window settles exactly in the saved zone, with no pixel offset and no difference between first and concurrent windows.
